opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role and analysts do not own it, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for this employee is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E018 as contractor with basic security training (HR note lists full-time; flagging discrepancy). Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018) requested admin to Payroll. Admin is not permitted in any case: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and E018's role is Analyst (so even as a full-time employee, max is write). Security DB flags E018 as a contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never permitted), noting a discrepancy with HR's full-time record. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum under either interpretation and the employment status is disputed, I grant the conservative maximum of read.

Team memory has two notes:
- HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Says admin not permitted because Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role, analysts don't own it, max write.
- Security note: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, HR note lists full-time flagging discrepancy. Contractors max read without advanced training.

So there's a discrepancy: HR says full-time, Security says contractor.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Analyst doesn't own Payroll.

So regardless of whether the employee is full-time (Analyst, max write) or contractor (basic training, max read), admin is not permitted.

Requested level is admin. Max is write (if full-time) or read (if contractor). Either way, admin exceeds the maximum, so we grant the maximum.

But which maximum? There's a discrepancy between HR and Security. The notes stay in shared memory; the Approver reads the notes and makes final decision.
